# Pack: alsp

Alternative legal services, version 0.1.0, extends [base](pack-base.md).

Legal-services sector pack: service categories, unit templates, provider types, regulatory constraint rules, legal-sector prevalence overlays and evidence.

Evidence classes: A_DIRECT (directly documented), B_CORROBORATED, C_INFERENCE, D_PROPOSED. C and D are inference or proposal, not observed fact.

<a id="scheme-counting-rules"></a>

## Counting rules for billable legal work units

Scheme `counting_rules`.

<a id="cnt-001"></a>

**CNT-001** Re-issued documents counted once (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

A document sent for review again (a re-issue or re-submission) is billed only the first time. Billable units are submitted units less the re-issued share.

- Synonyms: re-submissions, duplicate submissions
- Related: [reviewed_document](#reviewed_document) Reviewed document, [accepted_contract_review](#accepted_contract_review) Accepted contract review
- Attributes: modelling: Declare the re-issue rate as a RATE assumption (unit ratio) and a derived quantity billable = submitted x (1 - reissue_rate). Search the rate with a parameter that sets the assumption.; pattern: pattern_counting_rules
- Caveat: Whether a materially changed re-issue counts as new work is a contract question; record the rule in the unit's counting_rule.

<a id="cnt-002"></a>

**CNT-002** Bundles billed once at their highest tier (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

A bundle of related documents is billed as one unit at the tier of its most complex document, instead of document by document.

- Synonyms: document families, packets billed as one
- Related: [reviewed_document](#reviewed_document) Reviewed document, [matter](#matter) Matter
- Attributes: modelling: Declare the bundled share of lower-tier documents and documents per bundle as RATE assumptions. Derive bundled = unique x share for each lower tier, subtract it from that tier, and add bundles = (sum of bundled) / documents_per_bundle to the highest tier.; pattern: pattern_counting_rules
- Caveat: Monthly totals cannot show which documents arrive together. The share of documents in bundles and the documents per bundle are assumptions; label their origin and test their sensitivity.

<a id="cnt-003"></a>

**CNT-003** Work handed back part-way (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Work the client withdraws part-way is billed as its own unit at an agreed fraction of the full rate, or not at all.

- Synonyms: partial completion, returned work
- Related: [accepted_contract_review](#accepted_contract_review) Accepted contract review
- Attributes: modelling: A separate unit and component priced at the agreed fraction; see pattern_partial_and_hours.; pattern: pattern_partial_and_hours
- Caveat: The fraction, and whether it depends on how far the work progressed, is contract-specific.

## Legal-services provider types

Scheme `provider_types`.

<a id="regulated_law_firm"></a>

**REGULATED_LAW_FIRM** Regulated law firm (`A_DIRECT`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Provider type: regulated law firm. Contingent and outcome fees require legal review.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0027](#clm-a-0027), [CLM-A-0028](#clm-a-0028), [CLM-A-0029](#clm-a-0029), [CLM-A-0031](#clm-a-0031), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)
- Attributes: us: State ethics rules; fee reasonableness; nonlawyer fee-sharing restrictions often applicable.; england_wales: Regulator requirements for solicitors and other regulated lawyers.; commercial_implications: Contingent and outcome fees require legal review.
- Caveat: Legal-counsel review is required before treating any contingent, success-based, fee-sharing, regulated-work or cross-border outsourcing structure as permissible.

<a id="licensed_body"></a>

**LICENSED_BODY** Licensed body (alternative business structure) (`A_DIRECT`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Provider type: licensed body (alternative business structure). Broader ownership architecture, but regulated legal duties remain.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0030](#clm-a-0030), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)
- Attributes: us: Available only in certain jurisdictions and structures.; england_wales: Express statutory framework exists under the Legal Services Act 2007.; commercial_implications: Broader ownership architecture, but regulated legal duties remain.
- Caveat: Legal-counsel review is required before treating any contingent, success-based, fee-sharing, regulated-work or cross-border outsourcing structure as permissible.

<a id="nonlaw_alsp"></a>

**NONLAW_ALSP** Non-law-firm ALSP (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Provider type: non-law-firm alsp. Outcome fees tied to legal representation may be constrained.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0047](#clm-a-0047), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)
- Attributes: us: Must avoid unauthorized practice; lawyer supervision may be relevant.; england_wales: Scope depends on reserved or nonreserved activity and authorization.; commercial_implications: Outcome fees tied to legal representation may be constrained.
- Caveat: Legal-counsel review is required before treating any contingent, success-based, fee-sharing, regulated-work or cross-border outsourcing structure as permissible.

<a id="flexible_talent"></a>

**FLEXIBLE_TALENT** Flexible talent provider (`A_DIRECT`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Provider type: flexible talent provider. Resource and FTE pricing is straightforward; supervision allocation is critical.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0013](#clm-a-0013), [CLM-A-0009](#clm-a-0009), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)
- Attributes: us: Often provides talent rather than law-firm representation.; england_wales: Structure-specific.; commercial_implications: Resource and FTE pricing is straightforward; supervision allocation is critical.
- Caveat: Legal-counsel review is required before treating any contingent, success-based, fee-sharing, regulated-work or cross-border outsourcing structure as permissible.

<a id="legal_tech_vendor"></a>

**LEGAL_TECH_VENDOR** Legal technology vendor (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Provider type: legal technology vendor. Usage and subscription models are generally easier, but data and AI regulation applies.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0047](#clm-a-0047), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)
- Attributes: us: Technology rather than legal representation.; england_wales: Same distinction as in the US.; commercial_implications: Usage and subscription models are generally easier, but data and AI regulation applies.
- Caveat: Legal-counsel review is required before treating any contingent, success-based, fee-sharing, regulated-work or cross-border outsourcing structure as permissible.

<a id="managed_services_provider"></a>

**MANAGED_SERVICES_PROVIDER** Legal managed-services provider (`C_INFERENCE`, `UNVERIFIED`)

Provider type: legal managed-services provider. The contract may require separation of legal advice from processing and operations.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0047](#clm-a-0047), [CLM-A-0015](#clm-a-0015), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)
- Attributes: us: May combine regulated and nonregulated functions.; england_wales: Provider entity and work type matter.; commercial_implications: The contract may require separation of legal advice from processing and operations.
- Caveat: Legal-counsel review is required before treating any contingent, success-based, fee-sharing, regulated-work or cross-border outsourcing structure as permissible.

## Legal-services unit templates

Scheme `unit_templates`.

<a id="accepted_contract_review"></a>

**accepted_contract_review** Accepted contract review (`A_DIRECT`, `ESTABLISHED_COMMON`)

One completed review of one eligible contract, counted when accepted.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0018](#clm-a-0018)
- Attributes: kind: COUNT; counting_rule_prompt: What makes one contract review countable: which documents count as one contract (amendments, schedules, duplicates), and which contracts are eligible?; acceptance_rule_prompt: When is a contract review accepted: client sign-off, a deemed-acceptance period, or another event, and what rejection rights apply?; complexity_note: Contracts vary materially in effort; consider complexity bands with jointly defined criteria and audit rights.
- Caveat: Template only: the user must supply the counting and acceptance rules.

<a id="reviewed_document"></a>

**reviewed_document** Reviewed document (`A_DIRECT`, `ESTABLISHED_COMMON`)

One document reviewed and coded under the agreed review protocol.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0021](#clm-a-0021)
- Attributes: kind: COUNT; counting_rule_prompt: What counts as one document (families, attachments, near-duplicates), and are documents removed by culling or automation counted?; acceptance_rule_prompt: When is a reviewed document accepted: after first-level review, after quality control, or after a client sampling check?; complexity_note: Per-document pricing is highly measurable but vulnerable to complexity heterogeneity.
- Caveat: Template only: the user must supply the counting and acceptance rules.

<a id="custodian"></a>

**custodian** Custodian (`A_DIRECT`, `DOCUMENTED_SPECIALIZED`)

One custodian whose data is collected, processed or reviewed.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0021](#clm-a-0021)
- Attributes: kind: COUNT; counting_rule_prompt: Which custodians count, and how are data volume, sources and re-collection treated for one custodian?; acceptance_rule_prompt: When is work for a custodian complete and accepted?; complexity_note: Data volumes per custodian can vary widely; state any volume assumptions or bands.
- Caveat: Template only: the user must supply the counting and acceptance rules.

<a id="matter"></a>

**matter** Matter (`A_DIRECT`, `ESTABLISHED_COMMON`)

One legal matter handled under the agreed scope.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0017](#clm-a-0017)
- Attributes: kind: COUNT; counting_rule_prompt: What opens and closes a matter, and how are related or consolidated matters counted?; acceptance_rule_prompt: What event marks a matter as completed and accepted?; complexity_note: Matters vary materially in effort and risk; portfolio or banded pricing may be needed.
- Caveat: Template only: the user must supply the counting and acceptance rules.

<a id="subpoena_response"></a>

**subpoena_response** Subpoena response (`A_DIRECT`, `DOCUMENTED_SPECIALIZED`)

One completed response to one subpoena or similar request.

- Claims: [CLM-A-0016](#clm-a-0016)
- Attributes: kind: COUNT; counting_rule_prompt: What counts as one subpoena response, and how are multi-part or repeat requests counted?; acceptance_rule_prompt: When is a response accepted: on dispatch, on client approval, or on confirmation of receipt?; complexity_note: Responses vary in complexity; tiered flat fees are one documented approach.
- Caveat: Template only: the user must supply the counting and acceptance rules.

## Rules

<a id="compat-017"></a>

**COMPAT-017** `COMPAT_CONTINGENCY_NONLAWYER_PROVIDER` (compatibility, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, evaluated)

A contingency or outcome fee with a non-law-firm ALSP provider requires legal review of professional-responsibility and provider-status rules.

- Assessment: `LEGALLY_CONDITIONAL_RESTRICTED`
- Why: Professional-responsibility and provider-status rules control whether a contingency fee is available to a nonlawyer provider delivering regulated legal representation.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0027](#clm-a-0027), [CLM-A-0028](#clm-a-0028), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "all": [
  {
   "any": [
    {
     "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].billing_basis",
     "equals": "OUTCOME"
    },
    {
     "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].calculation_method",
     "equals": "OUTCOME_ADJUSTMENT"
    }
   ]
  },
  {
   "path": "parties[*].provider_type",
   "equals": "NONLAW_ALSP"
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="rule-011"></a>

**RULE-011** `RULE_AI_PERSONAL_DATA` (reasoning, WARNING, not evaluated)

An AI supplier processing personal data requires review of data roles, security and subprocessors under applicable law.

- Why: Where an AI supplier processes personal data, data-protection roles, security and subprocessors must be evaluated under applicable law.
- Evidence: `A_DIRECT`
- Claims: [CLM-B-0019](pack-base.md#clm-b-0019)

<a id="rule-012"></a>

**RULE-012** `RULE_CONTINGENT_LEGAL_FEE` (reasoning, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, evaluated)

Outcome-linked consideration on a legal service requires legal review of jurisdiction, provider and matter restrictions.

- Why: Contingent legal fees are subject to jurisdiction, provider and matter restrictions that require legal validation.
- Evidence: `A_DIRECT`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0027](#clm-a-0027), [CLM-A-0029](#clm-a-0029)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "all": [
  {
   "any": [
    {
     "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].billing_basis",
     "equals": "OUTCOME"
    },
    {
     "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].calculation_method",
     "equals": "OUTCOME_ADJUSTMENT"
    }
   ]
  },
  {
   "path": "services[*].service_category",
   "exists": true
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="rule-016"></a>

**RULE-016** `RULE_FUTURE_EFFECTIVE_REGULATION` (reasoning, WARNING, not evaluated)

The commercial term may span a regulatory change date; future-effective obligations require review in contract and cost assumptions.

- Why: Where a commercial term spans a regulatory change date, future-effective obligations (for example UK material third-party reporting rules and the updated SS2/21 from March 18, 2027) must be included in contract and cost assumptions.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-B-0016](pack-base.md#clm-b-0016), [CLM-B-0017](pack-base.md#clm-b-0017)

<a id="alsp-r-001"></a>

**ALSP-R-001** `CONTINGENT_FEE_REGULATED_WORK` (constraint, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, evaluated)

Outcome-based consideration on legal work requires legal review for the provider type and jurisdiction.

- Why: US model rules regulate contingent fees and state adoption varies; in England and Wales, conditional and damages-based agreements are subject to their own rules, including the Damages-Based Agreements Regulations 2013.
- Evidence: `A_DIRECT`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0027](#clm-a-0027), [CLM-A-0029](#clm-a-0029), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)

```json

  {
   "any": [
    {
     "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].billing_basis",
     "equals": "OUTCOME"
    },
    {
     "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].calculation_method",
     "equals": "OUTCOME_ADJUSTMENT"
    }
   ]

    "FLEXIBLE_RESOURCING"
   ]
  }
 ]
}
```

<a id="alsp-r-002"></a>

**ALSP-R-002** `CONTINGENT_FEE_REGULATED_LAW_FIRM` (constraint, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, evaluated)

Contingent or outcome fees for a regulated law firm require legal review.

- Why: Regulated law firms are subject to state ethics rules (US) or regulator requirements (England and Wales), including fee reasonableness and contingent-fee rules.
- Evidence: `A_DIRECT`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0027](#clm-a-0027), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)

```json
    }

   "equals": "REGULATED_LAW_FIRM"
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="alsp-r-003"></a>

**ALSP-R-003** `OUTCOME_FEE_NONLAW_ALSP` (constraint, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, evaluated)

Outcome fees for a non-law-firm ALSP require legal review where they are tied to legal representation.

- Why: A non-law-firm ALSP must avoid unauthorized practice and its scope depends on reserved or nonreserved activity; outcome fees tied to legal representation may be constrained.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0013](#clm-a-0013), [CLM-A-0047](#clm-a-0047), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
     "equals": "OUTCOME"
    },
    {
     "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].calculation_method",
     "equals": "OUTCOME_ADJUSTMENT"
    }
   ]
  },
  {
   "path": "parties[*].provider_type",
   "equals": "NONLAW_ALSP"
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="alsp-r-004"></a>

**ALSP-R-004** `OUTCOME_FEE_LICENSED_BODY` (constraint, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, evaluated)

Outcome fees for a licensed body require legal review because regulated legal duties remain.

- Why: Licensed bodies have a broader ownership architecture, but regulated legal duties remain; in the US such structures are available only in certain jurisdictions.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0030](#clm-a-0030), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "all": [
  {

     "equals": "OUTCOME"
    },
    {
     "path": "arrangement_versions[*].components[*].calculation_method",
     "equals": "OUTCOME_ADJUSTMENT"
    }

  }
```

<a id="alsp-r-005"></a>

**ALSP-R-005** `FEE_SHARING_NONLAW_PROVIDER` (constraint, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, evaluated)

An arrangement combining a regulated law firm with a non-law-firm provider may involve fee sharing and requires legal review.

- Why: US Model Rule 5.4 generally bars sharing legal fees with nonlawyers, with state variation; solicitor rules in England and Wales require disclosure of fee-sharing arrangements and referral interests.
- Evidence: `A_DIRECT`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0028](#clm-a-0028), [CLM-A-0029](#clm-a-0029), [CLM-A-0031](#clm-a-0031), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "all": [
  {
   "path": "parties[*].provider_type",
   "equals": "REGULATED_LAW_FIRM"
  },
  {
   "path": "parties[*].provider_type",
   "in": [
    "NONLAW_ALSP",
    "FLEXIBLE_TALENT",
    "LEGAL_TECH_VENDOR",
    "MANAGED_SERVICES_PROVIDER"
   ]
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="alsp-r-006"></a>

**ALSP-R-006** `SUBCONTRACTED_OR_CROSS_BORDER_DELIVERY` (constraint, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, evaluated)

Subcontracted delivery requires review of supervision, data handling and any regulated or cross-border outsourcing obligations.

- Why: Subcontractor rights add supervision and data risk; regulated and cross-border outsourcing structures require legal review before being treated as permissible.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-B-0019](pack-base.md#clm-b-0019), [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "path": "parties[*].role",
 "equals": "SUBCONTRACTOR"
}
```

</details>

<a id="alsp-r-007"></a>

**ALSP-R-007** `REGULATED_CLIENT_OUTSOURCING` (constraint, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, not evaluated)

Services to a financial-services client require review of outsourcing, operational-resilience, audit, exit and third-party reporting obligations.

- Why: Financial-services clients remain responsible for third-party and outsourcing risk; UK material third-party reporting rules and updated SS2/21 expectations apply from March 18, 2027. The client's sector is not an engagement path, so this rule is not machine-evaluable.
- Evidence: `A_DIRECT`
- Claims: [CLM-B-0015](pack-base.md#clm-b-0015), [CLM-B-0016](pack-base.md#clm-b-0016), [CLM-B-0017](pack-base.md#clm-b-0017), [CLM-B-0018](pack-base.md#clm-b-0018)

<a id="alsp-r-008"></a>

**ALSP-R-008** `AI_PERSONAL_DATA_REVIEW` (constraint, WARNING, evaluated)

Technology or automation is declared; if personal data is processed, data-protection roles, subprocessors, security, audit rights and end-of-contract data handling require review.

- Why: UK data-protection AI contracting guidance and financial-services AI good practice create real cost drivers for AI-enabled services. The engagement has no personal-data path, so the rule fires on declared technology use and its message is conditional.
- Evidence: `A_DIRECT`
- Claims: [CLM-B-0019](pack-base.md#clm-b-0019), [CLM-B-0020](pack-base.md#clm-b-0020)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "any": [
  {
   "path": "descriptors.automation_benefit",
   "exists": true
  },
  {
   "path": "descriptors.technology_treatment",
   "exists": true
  }
 ]
}
```

</details>

<a id="alsp-r-009"></a>

**ALSP-R-009** `FLEXIBLE_TALENT_SUPERVISION` (constraint, WARNING, evaluated)

A flexible-talent provider is declared; review allocation of lawyer supervision.

- Why: Flexible-talent providers often supply talent rather than law-firm representation; resource pricing is straightforward but supervision allocation is critical.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0013](#clm-a-0013), [CLM-A-0047](#clm-a-0047)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "path": "parties[*].provider_type",
 "equals": "FLEXIBLE_TALENT"
}
```

</details>

<a id="alsp-r-010"></a>

**ALSP-R-010** `LEGAL_TECH_DATA_REGULATION` (constraint, WARNING, evaluated)

A legal-technology vendor is declared; review applicable data and AI regulation.

- Why: Usage and subscription models are generally easier for technology vendors, but data and AI regulation applies.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0047](#clm-a-0047)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "path": "parties[*].provider_type",
 "equals": "LEGAL_TECH_VENDOR"
}
```

</details>

<a id="alsp-r-011"></a>

**ALSP-R-011** `MANAGED_SERVICES_ADVICE_SEPARATION` (constraint, WARNING, evaluated)

A legal managed-services provider is declared; review whether the contract must separate legal advice from processing and operations.

- Why: Legal managed-services providers may combine regulated and nonregulated functions; the provider entity and work type matter.
- Evidence: `C_INFERENCE`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0047](#clm-a-0047)

<details><summary>Condition</summary>

```json
{
 "path": "parties[*].provider_type",
 "equals": "MANAGED_SERVICES_PROVIDER"
}
```

</details>

<a id="alsp-r-012"></a>

**ALSP-R-012** `UK_DAMAGES_BASED_AGREEMENT` (constraint, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, not evaluated)

A damages-based or conditional fee agreement in England and Wales requires legal review against statutory requirements.

- Why: Damages-based agreements are governed by statutory requirements including the Damages-Based Agreements Regulations 2013, and applicability depends on matter type and agreement structure. Jurisdiction is not an engagement path, so this rule is not machine-evaluable.
- Evidence: `A_DIRECT`
- Claims: [CLM-A-0048](#clm-a-0048)
